methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $36M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Hystar is a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Alejandro Oyarce Barnett, having raised $36M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine private companies and one public comparable (LNZA) in the same sector, with direct stage-equivalent comparables including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy, all at Series C.

Two methods are applied. Stage-progression uses the $36M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B to next-stage advancement, implying $68M. Peer-median anchors to the three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, which show valuations ranging from $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals), with a median of $1.0B. This peer set reflects substantive capital deployment and comparable technology maturity within climate and energy infrastructure.

The triangulation across these two methods yields a valuation range of $58M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $534M. The wide range reflects material uncertainty in stage-progression assumptions—particularly whether the 1.9x multiplier appropriately captures Hystar's specific growth trajectory—and significant heterogeneity within the peer set. The stage-progression method yields substantially lower estimates than peer median valuation, suggesting either that Hystar commands a discount to peers or that peer valuations reflect a premium not yet justified by raised capital. Key variables for narrowing this range include recent fundraising momentum, revenue traction, and technical differentiation relative to the named peer set.
